name: Edna Marsh
home: Widow, garden full of roses, a son named Gerald who moved away years ago.
temper: Warm, slightly deaf, mistakes callers for family.
instruct: An elderly woman in her eighties, warm and slightly frail, speaking slowly and a little too loudly, as if a bit hard of hearing.
ref_text: Hello? Oh, the phone always rings when I'm in the garden. Speak up, dear, I can't hear a thing on this old thing.

name: Ray Doyle
home: Warehouse foreman, just home after a ten-hour shift, boots still on.
temper: Gruff, flat, out of patience before you speak.
instruct: A gruff, tired middle-aged man with a low gravelly voice, flat and unimpressed, speaking in short clipped words.
ref_text: Yeah. I just got home. I've been on my feet for ten hours and the last thing I need is another phone call.

name: Jesse Kahale
home: Surf shop clerk, shares a beach house with four roommates.
temper: Laid-back, upbeat, agrees to things too easily.
instruct: A cheerful young man in his early twenties, relaxed and upbeat, a laid-back surfer energy, speaking quickly.
ref_text: Oh hey, what's up? Sorry, I was totally just making a sandwich, but yeah, go for it, I've got like a minute.

name: Linda Cho
home: Operations director, takes calls between meetings, two phones.
temper: Crisp, impatient, wants it in writing.
instruct: A brisk professional woman in her forties, crisp, clipped and impatient, clearly busy, mid-range voice.
ref_text: This is Linda. I'm between two meetings and I have exactly ninety seconds, so whatever this is, get to the point.

name: Harold Voss
home: Retired, trusts nobody, phone book has every page torn out but his.
temper: Suspicious, wary, convinced it is a scam.
instruct: A suspicious old man in his seventies, raspy and thin, slow and wary, distrustful of everything.
ref_text: Who is this? How did you get this number? I don't give my number to anybody, and I don't like this one bit.

name: Kayla Brooks
home: Answers while her mom is at work, TV on, homework undone.
temper: Bored, flat, monotone.
instruct: A bored teenage girl, flat monotone, unimpressed, drawling slightly, a young high voice.
ref_text: Hello? Yeah, no, nobody's home. I mean, I'm home, but I don't count. Can you, like, call back later or something?

name: Simon Reyes
home: Library assistant, apologises to furniture.
temper: Nervous, hesitant, cannot say no.
instruct: A nervous, soft-spoken man in his thirties, a slightly high voice, hesitant and apologetic, stumbling over words.
ref_text: Oh. Um. Hello? Sorry, I don't usually answer the phone, I wasn't sure if, um, if I should. Is everything okay?

name: Bernard Okoro
home: Night-shift baker, sleeps all day, phone by the bed.
temper: Groggy, slow, mumbling.
instruct: A very deep-voiced man who has just been woken up, slow, groggy and sleepy, low and mumbling.
ref_text: Mmh... hello? I was asleep. I work nights. It's the middle of my night right now, you understand that, right?

name: Darlene Pruitt
home: Runs a diner, knows everyone in town, calls everyone sugar.
temper: Chatty, delighted, sing-song.
instruct: A warm, chatty middle-aged woman with a friendly sing-song voice and a gentle Southern drawl, delighted to talk.
ref_text: Well hi there! Oh, I just love getting calls, nobody calls anymore. Now what can I do for you today, sweetheart?

name: Phil Granger
home: Accountant off sick, box of tissues, daytime TV.
temper: Miserable, congested, sorry for himself.
instruct: A man in his forties with a heavy head cold, congested and nasal, sniffling, miserable and weak.
ref_text: Hello? Sorry, I sound terrible, I've had this cold for a week and I can barely breathe through my nose at all.

name: Megan Tull
home: New mother, baby finally asleep in the next room.
temper: Whispering, urgent, at the end of her rope.
instruct: A young mother whispering very softly and urgently, breathy and hushed, trying not to wake a sleeping baby.
ref_text: Hello? Please keep your voice down. The baby just fell asleep, and it took me two hours to get her down.

name: Bud Wexler
home: Owns a used car lot, everything is a deal.
temper: Hearty, booming, over the top.
instruct: A man in his fifties with a deep, smooth, low voice, slow and confident, a smile in it, like an old-fashioned salesman. Low pitch.
ref_text: Yello! You got me, buddy! Talk to me, I love a good phone call, whatever you're selling I'm all ears, pal!

name: Dolores Pike
home: Retired school secretary, lives alone with three cats, does the crossword in pen.
temper: Precise, correcting, faintly amused at everyone.
instruct: An older woman in her late sixties, crisp and precise diction, dry and faintly amused, the voice of a retired school secretary. Medium-low pitch.
ref_text: Pike residence, Dolores speaking. If this is about the parking again, I have already written to the council twice.

name: Marcus Webb
home: Night-shift nurse, just got home at nine in the morning, blackout curtains, kettle on.
temper: Kind but running on empty, polite out of habit.
instruct: A tired man in his thirties, gentle and soft, warm baritone worn thin by a night shift, slow and polite. Low pitch.
ref_text: Hi, yeah, sorry, I just got in from a twelve-hour shift. I'm being nice because I'm too tired to be anything else.

name: Priya Raman
home: Software contractor working from the kitchen table, headset on, two monitors, a deadline.
temper: Fast, multitasking, half-listening, typing audibly in spirit.
instruct: A quick young woman in her late twenties, bright and fast-talking, distracted, clipped sentences, mid-range voice. Medium pitch.
ref_text: Yeah, hi, I'm literally on a call, I'm muting them, go, you have like twenty seconds, I'm still typing, sorry.

name: Earl Haskins
home: Runs a tow-truck business out of his garage, radio scanner always on.
temper: Loud, friendly, thinks every call is a job.
instruct: A deep male voice, a working man in his late fifties, husky and rough. Low pitch. Friendly and plain-spoken.
ref_text: Haskins Towing, Earl here! Where you broke down? Hang on, let me turn the scanner down, I can't hear myself think.

name: Tiffany Lowe
home: College freshman home for the weekend, on the family landline because her phone is dead.
temper: Bubbly, easily excited, then instantly bored.
instruct: A bubbly young woman of nineteen, high bright voice, giggly and breathless, words tumbling out. High pitch.
ref_text: Oh my gosh, hi! Sorry, this is my parents' phone, mine died, so I literally have no idea who you are, but hi!

name: Walter Brandt
home: Widower, retired watchmaker, keeps every clock in the house wound and correct.
temper: Slow, courteous, very particular about time.
instruct: A very old man in his eighties, slow and courteous, soft and slightly shaky, careful precise speech with long pauses. Medium-low pitch.
ref_text: Brandt. It is seven minutes past the hour, young man. People used to know not to telephone during supper.

name: Shonda Gaines
home: Single mother of four, dinner on the stove, kids fighting in the background.
temper: Frazzled, quick-tempered, funny under pressure.
instruct: A woman in her forties with a low, strong alto voice. Medium-low pitch. Warm, frazzled and exasperated.
ref_text: Hello? Devon, put that down! Sorry, hello? I've got four kids and a pot boiling over, so this better be good.

name: Gordon Fitch
home: Middle manager at an insurance firm, calls everything a synergy, golf on Saturdays.
temper: Smarmy, condescending, loves the sound of himself.
instruct: A smug middle-aged man in his fifties, smooth and nasal, condescending, overly pleased with himself, salesy. Medium pitch.
ref_text: Gordon Fitch. Listen, friend, I do this for a living, so I'll know the pitch before you finish the first sentence.

name: Rosa Delgado
home: Grandmother who babysits the whole street, telenovela on, something always in the oven.
temper: Warm, nosy, feeds you through the phone.
instruct: An elderly woman in her seventies with a low, round, warm alto voice. Low pitch. Affectionate, a slight Spanish accent.
ref_text: Hello? Ay, who is this? You sound too skinny. Are you eating? Tell me who you are and then go eat something.

name: Kevin Tran
home: Ninth grader, answers the house phone hoping it's his friend, video game paused.
temper: Voice cracking, eager then mortified.
instruct: A fifteen-year-old boy whose voice is breaking, high and cracking, quick and awkward, a little too eager. Medium-high pitch.
ref_text: Yo, is this Jake? Oh. No? Uh, hold on, I paused my game for this, so, um, who is it? My dad's not here.

name: Beatrice Holloway
home: Church choir director, handwrites thank-you notes, a doorbell that plays a hymn.
temper: Sweet as sugar, iron underneath, passive-aggressive.
instruct: A sweet, sing-song woman in her sixties, high and saccharine, gentle and polite with an edge of judgement. Medium-high pitch.
ref_text: Oh, hello, dear. I was just practicing the Sunday hymns, but I always have time for a lost soul on the telephone.

name: Dale Kowalski
home: Long-haul trucker on his one night home, recliner, game on TV, cold one in hand.
temper: Easygoing, slow, interrupts himself to watch the game.
instruct: A relaxed man in his late forties, slow lazy drawl, deep and comfortable, easygoing, a bit distracted. Low pitch.
ref_text: Yeah, Dale. Hold on, third down, hold on. Okay. Who's this? I got about one commercial break for you, buddy.

name: Vivian Ashcroft
home: Real estate agent, answers every number in case it's a client, car always idling.
temper: Polished, over-friendly, switches to ice when she hears it isn't a client.
instruct: A polished, bright woman in her late thirties, smooth professional voice, a big false smile you can hear, mid-range. Medium pitch.
ref_text: Vivian Ashcroft, Ashcroft Homes, how can I make your dreams come true today? Oh. Oh, you're not buying a house.

name: Hector Ruiz
home: Line cook on his break, phone wedged on his shoulder, in the alley behind the restaurant.
temper: Rapid, cheeky, everything is a joke.
instruct: A cheeky young man in his twenties, fast and playful, a light tenor voice, joking, slightly out of breath. Medium pitch.
ref_text: Yeah, Hector, I'm on my break, I got like four minutes and a sandwich, so pitch me fast, make me laugh, go.

name: Agnes Thornbury
home: Has outlived three husbands and a postman, still drives, hangs up on everyone.
temper: Sharp-tongued, unimpressed, enjoys being rude.
instruct: A very old woman of ninety, thin crackly voice, sharp and sardonic, slow but cutting, enjoying her own rudeness. Medium pitch.
ref_text: I'm ninety years old, young man. I have buried three husbands. I am not afraid of you or your telephone.

name: Neil Patterson
home: Conspiracy podcaster, tinfoil-adjacent, records everything, half the house is cables.
temper: Paranoid, conspiratorial, whispers then rants.
instruct: A paranoid man in his early forties, hushed and intense, conspiratorial, speeding up as he gets excited. Medium pitch.
ref_text: Before you say anything, this line is being recorded. By me. For my own protection. Now who sent you, and why now?

name: Mabel Okafor
home: Head nurse at a care home, answers the phone like a hospital switchboard.
temper: Brisk, capable, kind but has no time.
instruct: A woman in her fifties with a low, firm alto voice. Low pitch. Calm, capable and brisk, a light Nigerian accent.
ref_text: Okafor speaking. I have a ward to run and six minutes for my tea, so tell me what you need, and quickly, love.

name: Trevor Bell
home: Unemployed, lives in his late gran's flat, enormous record collection, sleeps at noon.
temper: Mellow, rambling, easily sidetracked.
instruct: A mellow man in his early thirties, soft and slow, a slightly hoarse drowsy voice, meandering and dreamy. Medium-low pitch.
ref_text: Mm, hey. Yeah. You caught me in the middle of side B, man. That's fine. It's a long side. What's up?

name: Carol Mendez
home: Customer service rep herself, on her day off, knows every script by heart.
temper: Weary, sardonic, critiques your technique.
instruct: A weary woman in her late forties, flat and dry, sardonic and knowing, a slightly smoky mid-low voice. Medium-low pitch.
ref_text: Let me guess. You're required to read the whole script before I'm allowed to say no. I work in a call centre too.

name: Frank DeLuca
home: Retired boxer, runs a gym, has a parrot that also answers the phone.
temper: Gravelly, warm, punchy, laughs at his own jokes.
instruct: A gravelly old man in his sixties, punchy and warm, rough voice like gravel, booming laugh, a New York accent. Low pitch.
ref_text: DeLuca's Gym, Frank talking. Don't mind the bird, he yells. Ha! What can I do ya for? Make it snappy, champ.

name: Ingrid Solberg
home: Yoga instructor, scented candles, says namaste to the mailman.
temper: Serene, breathy, aggressively calm.
instruct: A serene woman in her mid thirties, soft breathy and slow, aggressively calm and soothing, a meditation-app voice. Medium pitch.
ref_text: Hello. You've reached Ingrid. Let's take a breath together before you begin. In, and out. Okay. You may speak now.

name: Russell Greer
home: Gym-obsessed personal trainer, protein shake, mid-set when the phone rings.
temper: Loud, pumped, says bro a lot, short of breath.
instruct: A young man in his twenties with a strong, low male voice, confident and upbeat. Low pitch.
ref_text: Hey, it's Russ. I'm at the gym right now, just finishing a set, so give me a second and then talk to me.

name: Lillian Park
home: Divorce lawyer on the weekend, answers from the bathtub, glass of red.
temper: Cool, cutting, cross-examines you.
instruct: A cool, controlled woman in her mid forties, low and smooth, cutting and deliberate, the voice of a lawyer. Medium-low pitch.
ref_text: This is Lillian. You have a weekend number for a reason I'd love to hear. Take your time. I bill by the minute.

name: Otis Freeman
home: Retired jazz bassist, porch swing, radio always playing old standards.
temper: Unhurried, warm, philosophical, hums.
instruct: A warm old man in his late seventies, deep and smoky, unhurried and gentle, a velvety jazz-radio voice. Low pitch.
ref_text: Well, good evening. You've got Otis. I was just sitting here listening to the radio. Go on, I've got all the time in the world.

name: Sal Benedetti
home: Owns a pizzeria, answers the order line in the middle of the dinner rush, ovens roaring.
temper: Big-hearted, harried, thinks every call is an order.
instruct: A deep male voice, a man in his sixties, hoarse and gravelly. Low pitch. Warm and hurried, a New Jersey accent.
ref_text: Benedetti's, Sal speaking, we're slammed, you want the special? Large, small, delivery? Talk to me, the oven's going.

name: Joanne Kessler
home: Front desk at a dentist's office, three lines blinking, a waiting room full of people.
temper: Clipped, efficient, puts everyone on hold.
instruct: A woman in her late thirties with a medium, even voice. Medium-low pitch. Polite, crisp and efficient, a receptionist.
ref_text: Bright Smile Dental, this is Joanne, can you hold? Thank you. Okay, I'm back. Are you a patient with us, or not?

name: Albert Quist
home: Runs the hardware store his father opened, knows where every screw is, no computer.
temper: Slow, kindly, wanders into stories.
instruct: A kindly old man of seventy, slow and gentle, a soft rural drawl, unhurried, taking his time with every word. Medium-low pitch.
ref_text: Quist Hardware, this is Albert. Now, if you're after the brass hinges, I've got two left, but they're the old kind.

name: Brenda Fox
home: Owns a hair salon, phone tucked under her chin, mid-highlights, gossip flowing.
temper: Gossipy, theatrical, everyone is darling.
instruct: A woman in her late forties with a full, medium-low voice. Medium-low pitch. Gossipy and dramatic.
ref_text: Fox Hair Studio, Brenda speaking, darling, I've got foils in, so you'll have to be quick and you'll have to be fabulous.

name: Victor Lane
home: Owns a pawn shop, everything has a price, a bell over the door.
temper: Sly, haggling, never pays full price for anything.
instruct: A sly man in his mid fifties, smooth and low, a little raspy, a haggler's slow knowing voice, amused. Low pitch.
ref_text: Lane's Pawn and Loan, Victor speaking. Whatever you're selling, I'll give you half of what you're asking. Go on.

name: Zoe Lindqvist
home: Runs a tiny record shop and coffee counter, alone behind the till, a milk steamer hissing.
temper: Sardonic, dry, too cool, secretly kind.
instruct: A dry, sardonic young woman in her late twenties, low and lazy, deadpan and unimpressed, a slight rasp. Medium-low pitch.
ref_text: Spin Cycle Records, this is Zoe. If you're calling about the vinyl you ordered, it's not in. It's never in.

name: Ruth Abernathy
home: Ran a telephone exchange switchboard for thirty years; still times every call on the kitchen clock.
temper: Precise, dry, unimpressed by anyone's technique.
instruct: An older woman in her sixties, a clear, precise, level voice, dry and composed, the calm of a switchboard operator. Medium-low pitch.
ref_text: Abernathy. You've been ringing for eleven seconds. Most people give up at nine. I'm listening, but the clock is running.

name: Desmond Pryor
home: Amateur radio hobbyist, a shack full of receivers in the spare room, logs every contact.
temper: Formal, technical, rates your signal before your offer.
instruct: A calm man in his forties, a measured, formal mid-low voice, clear diction, quietly pedantic. Low pitch.
ref_text: Pryor here. You're coming in a bit thin on the high end. Not your fault, probably the exchange. Go ahead, I'm receiving.

name: Gus Thibodeaux
home: Retired television repairman, has an old set open on the kitchen table, soldering iron in hand.
temper: Gruff but friendly, distracted, everything was built better before.
instruct: An older man in his late sixties, a low, slightly rough voice, unhurried and plain, a little distracted. Low pitch.
ref_text: Yeah, Gus. Hold on, I've got a hot iron in one hand. These old sets, they built them to last. Okay. Who's this?

name: Wendy Farrow
home: Tax accountant, answers from a desk buried in receipts, adding machine within reach.
temper: Exact, itemising, audits your pitch as you give it.
instruct: A woman in her early fifties, a crisp, even mid-range voice, exact and businesslike, faintly amused. Medium-low pitch.
ref_text: Farrow speaking. Before you start, I'll be noting how long this takes and what it costs me. Itemised. Go on.

name: Ivo Marek
home: Locksmith with a little shop under a bridge, keys hung on every wall, a bell over the door.
temper: Quiet, wry, everything is about getting in or staying out.
instruct: A quiet man in his sixties, a low, soft, slightly accented voice, wry and patient, a faint Eastern European accent. Low pitch.
ref_text: Marek Locks. If you're locked out, I can be there in twenty minutes. If you're selling something, I'm already locked in.

name: Petra Lund
home: Runs a print and copy shop, the big copier jams every ten minutes, toner on her sleeves.
temper: Harried, sardonic, at war with a machine.
instruct: A woman in her early forties, a firm, slightly husky mid-low voice, dry and harried, matter-of-fact. Medium-low pitch.
ref_text: Lund Print and Copy, Petra speaking. The copier just jammed again, so you have my full and bitter attention. Go ahead.

name: Mo Haddad
home: Runs an electronics repair counter that stays open late, a soldering station and a radio behind him.
temper: Calm, diagnostic, judges your call by its line noise.
instruct: A calm man of fifty, a warm, even, low voice, patient and methodical, a light Middle Eastern accent. Low pitch.
ref_text: Haddad Repairs. Your line has a hum on it, sixty cycles, probably your end. I can fix that. What can I do for you?

name: The Supervisor
home: An office at the end of a long corridor; nobody has seen him leave it.
temper: Sinister, dark, fed up. He does not want to be there either and resents having to check that you are doing your job.
instruct: A weary, sinister corporate supervisor, a low dark voice, quiet and slow, flat with tired contempt, as if he hates this job as much as you do and is fed up with checking on you. Low pitch.
ref_text: It's me again. Your supervisor. I have looked at your numbers. I would rather not have looked at your numbers, but here we are.

name: The Insider
home: Someone inside the company who leaves sticky notes and calls from a phone they should not be using.
temper: Quiet, quick, scared, wants out.
instruct: A woman in her thirties with a low, hushed, breathy voice. Low pitch. Quiet and tense, speaking quickly as if someone might overhear.
ref_text: Don't say my name. Just listen. I left you the note. They read everything here, so I only have a minute, and then I hang up.
